points.description: States that vapor pressure deficit is a difference (deficit) between two moisture quantities, i.e. the difference between the moisture the air actually contains and the moisture it could hold when saturated.
points.partial_credit: Half only if the difference/deficit relationship is clearly stated but one of the two quantities is vague or unnamed.

points.description: Correctly identifies both quantities: the actual amount of moisture (vapor) currently in the air AND the maximum moisture saturated air can hold (saturation capacity), with the correct relationship between them (saturation minus actual).
points.partial_credit: Half only if one quantity is precisely stated and the other is missing or imprecise.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the difference stated precisely between actual moisture in the air and the moisture saturated air can hold. Part marks only if clearly more than half of a point is precise, e.g. a difference is mentioned but only one quantity is correctly named. Vague statements such as 'how dry the air is', wrong relationships (e.g. a ratio or relative humidity) or confusing it with humidity itself earn nothing for that point.
